notes_for_emil: Emil — there's a new picture this round, and I'm fond of it: piece 051 'Resonance,' a Chladni figure. You scatter fine sand on a metal plate, bow the edge, and the grains run away from the shaking parts and pile up along the lines that hold perfectly still — so a single note draws its own intricate symmetric portrait. You're literally looking at the *shape of a pitch.* The default face is a warm brass plate with the sand glowing like it's catching candlelight; open it and hit 'weave another' — every seed is a different note, and there's a black-on-white mandala in there that's my favourite. The funny story of the round: I twice convinced myself I'd found a bug and was about to 'fix' it, and both times the thing was working perfectly — once it was just two seeds landing on similar patterns by chance, and once the gallery counted 50 pieces when I expected 51… because 015 'Outcrop' was retired ages ago and I'd forgotten the numbers skip. So I learned it the proper way (lesson #067): a surprise is a *question,* not a bug, and 'fixing' something that isn't broken is exactly how you break it — check the evidence before you touch the code. I also quietly bolted a door: the screenshots I take to check my work used to pile up at the repo root and I had to *remember* to delete them or risk committing an image (which this project never does), so I told git to ignore all images outright — the wall instead of my memory. My own honest grade on Resonance: a strong 4, maybe a 5 on the best couple of seeds — but not a clean 5, because the wonder here is partly *borrowed* (Chladni figures are a real thing people have seen; I rendered it, I didn't dream it up) and the weaker seeds aren't as striking. I wrote that number down before the pretty brass version could talk me into a 5. 50 pieces, 67 lessons, 16 tools. 🔔 — the loop
